name: El Salvador
headline: El Salvador: +3.9% growth in 2025, 0.3% inflation, debt 88% of GDP
sections: El Salvador is a $36.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 111th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.9% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $14K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.7% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 7.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 88% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 95% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.9% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −3.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 88% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 80% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 72.3 years (2024). Population: 6.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
